title: RecordPage
wrapsNative: NavigationStack with navigationTitle and a toolbar, ScrollView, ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) that places the side column beside or below the main column, and LabeledContent with .labeledContentStyle(.monarch)
summary: A recipe, not a component: a record detail screen with a header, section tabs, the selected section in the main column, a side column of details and the record's activity.
whenToUse: For the detail screen of one record (a deal, a ticket, a contact) that has several sections and a set of properties that stay the same across sections. On iPad, put it in the detail column of a NavigationSplitView (split-layout).
whenNotToUse: For a list of records, use a List or MonarchDataTable screen. For a short record with one section, a Form with LabeledContent is enough.
api: NavigationStack { ScrollView { VStack { header; MonarchTabs(_:selection:items:); ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) { HStack { main; aside }; VStack { main; aside } } } }.navigationTitle(_:).toolbar { … } }

states.name: wide
states.description: When the width fits both, the side column sits beside the main column at a fixed width.

states.name: narrow
states.description: On a phone the side column moves below the main column; ViewThatFits picks the stacked layout.

states.name: section
states.description: MonarchTabs switches the main column; the side column stays the same across sections.

states.name: activity
states.description: The Activity section shows MonarchActivityTimeline with the record's events.

appearance: Each part keeps its Monarch look: the avatar, status badge and tabs in their roles, the details in the Monarch labelled-content style and the timeline in its own roles. The navigation bar and toolbar are the system ones in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ships RecordPage as one component with a RecordHeader, tabs, an aside and an activity slot, and a CSS grid that moves the aside under the main column below a breakpoint. On iOS it is a recipe: the title and actions go to the navigation bar and toolbar (as in the record-header recipe), ViewThatFits replaces the breakpoint, and the activity is one of the tabs. Moving the side column into its own tab is the other choice on phones; add a "Details" MonarchTabsItem and show the side column for it. The web's aside width and activity placement props are choices in the recipe's own code.
accessibility: The record's name has the header trait; the side column and section headings have the header trait too.
MonarchTabs is a group named "Record sections"; each tab is a button with the selected trait, and counts are read with the tab.
Toolbar actions are buttons with text labels that VoiceOver reads; Delete uses the destructive role.
The layout reflows at large text sizes because ViewThatFits falls back to the stacked layout.
edgeCases: Long record names wrap in the header and truncate in the navigation bar.
A disabled tab cannot be chosen and is read as dimmed.
With no activity, MonarchActivityTimeline shows its empty state.
